phase_1_state.question: #325: did the quarterback disposition land before the poller's first in-season starter change, as the plan required?
phase_1_state.answer: Yes. Milestone 'Phase 1' closed 2026-09-17, with every ticket landed (#300-#304, #324, #328-#331) before week 2. The disposition is tied to the line-move coefficient with verdict() tested before the first row.
phase_1_state.but: The instrument has no 2026 input (V2, #420): its events come from a file pinned on 2026-09-13, and its frozen prices from an archive whose last poll was 2026-09-06 (#383). The study's NOT-RUNNABLE at this trigger is the state #325 said to expect. It is not a finding about Phase 1 either way. The finding is that, as built, it can never become runnable in 2026, and that its run line reports '2026: 0 changes' as if that were a fact about the season.

new_findings.verified: direct for the symptom; mechanism inferred from code (payload not read)
new_findings.title: The lineup call has been blank since 2026-09-26: availability reads every healthy player as missing the weeks already played
evidence: roster.availability treats the roster's largest total/avg ratio as a full slate. All four availability tests build the preseason shape only (every ratio a full season).
The page renders 'Withheld as unavailable: <14 names> ... short of a full slate' and 'No lineup could be filled'. The manifest says ok.
new_findings.why_it_matters: It is the one in-season decision the page makes for the operator, and it has been absent for weeks 3 (Saturday), 4 and 5 with no stale flag.

new_findings.verified: direct (M-V2; nfeloqb.PINNED_SHA256; docs/qb-adjustment.md documents the pin's effect on the live path only)
new_findings.title: Phase 1's line-move study cannot see a 2026 event, and prints 0 as a fact
Where the line-move study's in-season starter changes come from: (A) advance the pin, (B) play-by-play, (C) wait for 2027. Recommendation (B). blocked_by #383.
new_findings.note: One option considered and dropped before filing: reconstructing frozen prices from the git history of published preds. A week's preds file is first committed on the Wednesday after the previous week's games, which is too late for a price that must predate the change.

new_findings.verified: direct (publish.track_record writes n_preregistered=0 as a literal; M-V3)
new_findings.title: The track record calls 64 slate-committed 2026 predictions a backtest
The published coverage verdict is a fixed 2021-2025 backtest re-measured twice a week, and 2026's played weeks never enter
new_findings.also: The track record embeds the previous run's measurement, and float noise puts a change to state/ into every slate commit.

new_findings.title: The Big Ten capture has failed 25 of 25 runs and missed 20+ deadlines: CFB_WEEK_ONE was never set, and the miss record dies at git add
new_findings.also: cfbd.json has read fetched:false on every slate since 2026-09-09. The operator step (setting the repository variable) is the maintainer's.

blocking.reasoning: #326's hold rule exists to stop a modelling change landing on an unsound basis. S1 was blocking because the gate that decides modelling changes was wrong. None of V1-V6 changes how a Phase 2 or Phase 3 change would be decided. They are repairs to what the page publishes now, and none of them is behind the freeze. Holding #326 for them would delay nothing they need. #326 is not commented on and not closed: lifting it is the maintainer's act.

what_is_strong: The precondition is a check, not a sentence. hub.audit_ready answered the exact question this audit is gated on, reads only site/data, and its 64-of-64 answer agrees with track_record's own per-season count. Its refusal branch was not exercised by this audit.
Freeze-at-kickoff on published prices works in production: the games already played in week 3 kept their 09-23 price on the 09-26 run.

The slate's refresh job has not failed since 2026-09-16: every refresh since (five scheduled, one dispatch) published a slate commit. The 10-06 run's steps were read: contract subset before the commit, coverage gate after it, all green.
survivor.json labels its plan unread-state, so it does not claim to be the pool's record (#380).
The lock() refusal itself is correct: with the pool emptied, it names the withheld players and publishes no comparison rather than a wrong one. V1 is upstream of it.

replan.principle: Re-planned on what the artifacts show. The 2026 page's only in-season decision (the lineup call) is broken, the money layer has no 2026 subject, and Phase 2's subject reaches no published artifact. So the repairs go first, Phase 3 shrinks, and Phase 2 is ordered behind the gate-rule decision its verdicts depend on.
